newsitem.title: UK: Anglian gives details of failed Manila bid.
newsitem.headline: Anglian gives details of failed Manila bid.

text.p: British water and sewerage company Anglian Water Plc said it had envisaged returns of around 50 million pounds over 25 years in its failed bid for a contract to supply water and sewage systems to Manila in the Philippines.
"We saw returns over 25 years of around 50 million pounds for the east zone contract," a spokesman for the company said.
He said the contribution to post-tax profits would have worked out at around two to three million annually.
Anglian, in a consortium with Australia Water Technologies Pty Ltd and Metro Pacific Corp, bid at a tariff of 64.5 percent of the existing price of 8.78 pesos per litre.
The winning bid was made at 26.38 percent by a consortium which included Britain's United Utilities, Bechtel Corp of the U.S. and local conglomerate Ayala Corp.
Anglian had expected to make an equity investment of around $14 million if it had won the contract, the spokesman said, and was working on a target of 20 percent post-tax returns on that.
"We had decided what sort of rate of return we were looking for and thought our tender was about right," he said.
